problem_text:
A logistics firm aims to devise a cargo-handling improvement plan to reduce total shipment delay hours across several distribution hubs. Initially, no procedural adjustments have been implemented.

The operational characteristics of each hub are as follows:
* For Hub A, delay factor is 2.523, cargo volume is 161.05.
* For Hub B, delay factor is 0.914, cargo volume is 121.232.
* For Hub C, delay factor is 1.594, cargo volume is 237.134.
* For Hub D, delay factor is 1.527, cargo volume is 162.232.
* For Hub E, delay factor is 2.191, cargo volume is 183.503.
* For Hub F, delay factor is 1.094, cargo volume is 127.367.

To mitigate delays, several procedural enhancements are available, each characterized by a specific reduction efficiency:
* By implementing Procedure Alpha, delays will be reduced by 25%.
* By implementing Procedure Beta, delays will be reduced by 52%.
* By implementing Procedure Gamma, delays will be reduced by 23%.
* By implementing Procedure Delta, delays will be reduced by 61%.
* By implementing Procedure Epsilon, delays will be reduced by 14%.
* By implementing Procedure Zeta, delays will be reduced by 11%.

Applying a procedural enhancement to a hub incurs an additional cost per unit of cargo volume. The cost structure for all hub–procedure combinations is summarized below:

| Hub \ Procedure | Alpha | Beta | Gamma | Delta | Epsilon | Zeta |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Hub A | 97.719 | 63.537 | 82.556 | 110.217 | 193.591 | 165.209 |
| Hub B | 162.239 | 36.296 | 57.501 | 131.824 | 176.082 | 115.363 |
| Hub C | 29.492 | 170.72 | 171.722 | 64.162 | 154.992 | 61.83 |
| Hub D | 182.008 | 37.996 | 93.12 | 189.819 | 52.187 | 95.714 |
| Hub E | 76.421 | 15.067 | 20.119 | 105.381 | 54.798 | 198.96 |
| Hub F | 81.233 | 15.356 | 186.857 | 169.443 | 133.493 | 160.362 |

Please determine how to apply procedural enhancements to each hub (hubs may adopt multiple procedures concurrently), and note that a hub may also remain partially unimproved if necessary. The objective is to ensure that the total shipment delay hours are reduced by at least a proportion P = 0.269 of the initial baseline, while minimizing the total operational cost.
